definitions.explanation: The act of fundamentally changing and renewing systems, institutions, or practices. Most famously associated with the Taika Reform ({大化|たいか}の{改新|かいしん}) of 645 CE, one of the most important events in early Japanese history.

examples.japanese: ⟦{制度|せいど}→制度：03291_seido⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{改新|かいしん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{必要|ひつよう}→必要：00846_hitsuyou⟧だ。
examples.english: Reform of the system is necessary.

examples.japanese: {大化|たいか}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{改新|かいしん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{歴史|れきし}→歴史：02267_rekishi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{転換点|てんかんてん}→転換点：09951_tenkanten⟧だった。
examples.english: The Taika Reform was a turning point in Japanese history.

examples.japanese: ⟦{組織|そしき}→組織：03320_soshiki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{改新|かいしん}⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧、⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{合|あ}った→合う：10466_au⟧⟦{形|かたち}→形：02193_katachi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{必要|ひつよう}→必要：00846_hitsuyou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: We need to reform the organization and bring it into a form suited to the times.

notes:
Compound of {改|かい} (change, reform) and {新|しん} (new). Most strongly associated with {大化|たいか}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{改新|かいしん} (Taika Reform, 645 CE), which centralized political power under the emperor and is a key topic in Japanese history education.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {大化|たいか}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{改新|かいしん}: the Taika Reform (645 CE)
- ⟦{制度|せいど}→制度：03291_seido⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{改新|かいしん}: institutional reform
- {改新|かいしん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{行|おこな}う→行う：01238_okonau⟧: to carry out reform

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{改革|かいかく}→改革：04815_kaikaku⟧: reform — the most common modern word for reform, used broadly
- ⟦{刷新|さっしん}→刷新：07520_sasshin⟧: renovation, overhaul — implies sweeping, dramatic renewal
- ⟦{革新|かくしん}→革新：05617_kakushin⟧: innovation, reform — emphasizes radical or progressive change
- ⟦{維新|いしん}→維新：13869_ishin⟧: restoration, revolution — used historically (⟦{明治|めいじ}{維新|いしん}→明治維新：16286_meijiishin⟧, Meiji Restoration)
